{{short description|French researcher in statistical learning}}
{{Orphan|date=March 2021}}

[[File:Éric Moulines - 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Eric Moulines in April 2019]]
'''Éric Moulines''' (born in [[Bordeaux]] on 24 January 1963) is a French researcher in [[Machine learning|statistical learning]] and [[signal processing]]. He received the silver medal from the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]] in 2010,<ref name="cnrs-ins2i" /> and was appointed a Fellow of the [[European Association for Signal Processing]] in 2012<ref name="eurasip-fellows" /> and of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2016,<ref name="ims-fellows-2016" /> and was elected a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 2017.<ref name="academie-sciences" /> He is General Engineer of the [[Corps des Mines]] (X81).<ref name="annales-mines-bio">{{cite web|title=Bio MOULINES, Éric|url=https://annales-des-mines.org/bio-moulines-eric/|website=Les Annales des Mines|access-date=21 April 2026|language=fr}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Éric Moulines entered the [[École Polytechnique|École polytechnique]] in 1981, then went to study at [[Télécom ParisTech]].

He began his career at the [[Centre national d'études des télécommunications]] where he worked on [[speech synthesis]] from text. He is involved in the development of new waveform synthesis methods called PSOLA (pitch synchronous overlap and add).<ref>Eric Moulines, Francis Charpentier, « Pitch-synchronous waveform processing techniques for text-to-speech synthesis using diphones », ''Speech Communication'', 1990, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 453–467</ref>

After defending his thesis in 1990,<ref name="bnf-thesis">{{cite web|title=Algorithmes de codage et de modifications des paramètres prosodiques pour la synthèse de parole à partir du texte|url=http://ark.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb12947497t|website=Catalogue général|publisher=Bibliothèque nationale de France|access-date=21 April 2026|language=fr}}</ref> he joined the [[École nationale supérieure des télécommunications|École Nationale Supérieure des Télécommunications]] (now [[Télécom ParisTech]]).<ref name="cnrs-ins2i" /> He then became interested in different problems of statistical signal processing. In particular, it contributes to the development of subspaces methods for the identification of multivariate linear systems<ref>E Moulines, P Duhamel, JF Cardoso, S Mayrargue, « Subspace methods for the blind identification of multichannel FIR filters », ''IEEE Transactions on signal processing,'', 1995, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 516–525</ref> and source separation<ref>Belouchrani, Adel and Abed-Meraim, Karim and Cardoso, J-F and Moulines, Eric, « A blind source separation technique using second-order statistics », ''IEEE Transactions on signal processing'', 1997, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 434–444</ref> and develops new [[algorithm]]s for adaptive system estimation.

He became a full professor at Télécom ParisTech in 1996.<ref name="cnrs-ins2i" /> He received his [[Habilitation à diriger des recherches]] (authorisation to direct research) in 2006.<ref name="edite-paris">{{cite web|title=Fiche de MOULINES Eric|url=https://myedb.edite-de-paris.fr/Fiche/19419/|website=myEDB|publisher=EDITE de Paris|access-date=21 April 2026|language=fr}}</ref> He then devoted himself mainly to the application of Bayesian methods with applications in signal processing and statistics. In 2025 he joined the faculty of [[Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence]] (MBZUAI) in Abu Dhabi.<ref name="sifted-mbzuai">{{cite news|last=Leprince-Ringuet|first=Daphné|title=How the 'Stanford of the Middle East' is attracting top European researchers|url=https://sifted.eu/articles/mbzuai-europe-researchers|work=Sifted|date=14 February 2025|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>

== Scientific work ==
He is interested in the inference of latent variable models<ref>O Cappé, E Moulines, « On‐line expectation–maximization algorithm for latent data models », ''Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B (Statistical Methodology)'', 2009, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 593–613</ref> and in particular [[Hidden Markov model|hidden Markov chains]],<ref>R Douc, E Moulines, T Rydén, « Asymptotic properties of the maximum likelihood estimator in autoregressive models with Markov regime », ''The Annals of statistics'', 2004, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 2254–2304</ref><ref>O. Cappé, E. Moulines, T. Ryden, « Inference in Hidden Markov Models », ''Springer Series in Statistics'', 2006</ref> and non-linear state models (non-linear filtering)<ref name=":0">R Douc, A Garivier, E Moulines, J Olsson, « Sequential Monte Carlo smoothing for general state space hidden Markov models », ''The Annals of Applied Probability'', 2011, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 2109–2145</ref><ref name=":1">R Douc, E Moulines, D Stoffer, « Nonlinear time series: Theory, methods and applications with R examples », ''Chapman and Hall/CRC'', 2014</ref> In particular, it contributes to filtering methods using interacting particle systems.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> He was more generally interested in the inference of partially observed Markovian models, coupling estimation and simulation problems with Monte Carlo Markov Chain Methods (MCMC). He has also developed numerous theoretical tools for the convergence analysis of MCMC algorithms, obtaining fundamental results on the long time behaviour of Markov chains.<ref>C Andrieu, É Moulines, « On the ergodicity properties of some adaptive MCMC algorithms », ''The Annals of Applied Probability'', 2006, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 1462–1505</ref><ref>R Douc, E Moulines, P Priouret, P Soulier, « Markov Chains », ''Springer'', 2018</ref><ref>A Durmus, E Moulines, « Nonasymptotic convergence analysis for the unadjusted Langevin algorithm », ''The Annals of Applied Probability'', 2017, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 1551–1587</ref>

Since 2005, he has been working on statistical learning problems, including the analysis of [[stochastic]] optimization algorithms.<ref>A Garivier, E Moulines, « On upper-confidence bound policies for switching bandit problems », ''International Conference on Algorithmic Learning'', 2011, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 174–188</ref><ref>E Moulines, FR Bach, « Non-asymptotic analysis of stochastic approximation algorithms for machine learning », ''Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems'', 2011, <abbr>pp.</abbr> 451–459</ref>

He joined the Centre de mathématiques appliquées de l'École polytechnique<ref>{{cite journal|title=Le statisticien historique : Éric Moulines, professeur à l'École polytechnique|url=https://www.usinenouvelle.com/article/le-statisticien-historique-eric-moulines-professeur-a-l-ecole-polytechnique.N648643|website=usinenouvelle.com|date=7 February 2018 |last1=Nouvelle |first1=L'Usine }}</ref> as a professor in 2015. He is interested in [[Bayesian inference|Bayesian]] inference from large scale models, with applications in [[uncertainty quantification]] in statistical learning.

Since 2022, Moulines has led the OCEAN (On IntelligenCE And Networks) project, a six-year [[European Research Council|ERC]] Synergy Grant on [[federated learning]] and decentralised artificial intelligence, jointly with [[Michael I. Jordan]] ([[University of California, Berkeley|UC Berkeley]]), [[Christian P. Robert]] ([[Paris Dauphine University|Université Paris Dauphine-PSL]]) and [[Gareth Roberts (statistician)|Gareth Roberts]] ([[University of Warwick]]).<ref name="erc-syg-2022" />

== Honours and awards ==
* [[European Research Council|ERC]] Synergy Grant in 2022, with [[Michael I. Jordan|Michael Jordan]] (UC Berkeley), [[Christian P. Robert|Christian Robert]] ([[Paris Dauphine University|Université Paris Dauphine-PSL]]) and [[Gareth Roberts (statistician)|Gareth Roberts]] ([[University of Warwick]]), for the OCEAN (On IntelligenCE And Networks) project on federated learning<ref name="erc-syg-2022">{{cite web|title=ERC Synergy Grants 2022 List of proposals selected for funding|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2022-10/erc_2022_syg.pdf|website=European Research Council|format=PDF|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
* Chevalier (Knight) of the [[Ordre national du Mérite|National Order of Merit]] (24 November 2021)<ref name="onm-2021">{{cite web|title=Décret du 24 novembre 2021 portant promotion et nomination dans l'ordre national du Mérite|url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/id/JORFTEXT000044361959|website=Légifrance|publisher=République française|access-date=21 April 2026|language=fr}}</ref>
* Technical Achievement Award of the European Association for Signal Processing (EURASIP) in 2020<ref name="eurasip-awards">{{cite web|title=Society Awards|url=https://eurasip.org/society-awards/|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
* Elected member of the French Academy of Sciences on 5 December 2017, in the Mechanical and Computer Sciences section<ref name="academie-sciences">{{cite web|title=Eric Moulines|url=https://academie-sciences.fr/en/eric-moulines|website=Académie des sciences|access-date=21 April 2026|language=en}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]] in 2016<ref name="ims-fellows-2016">{{cite web|title=IMS Fellows 2016|url=https://imstat.org/2016/07/01/ims-fellows-2016/|website=Institute of Mathematical Statistics|date=1 July 2016|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
* Fellow of the [[European Association for Signal Processing]] (EURASIP) in 2012<ref name="eurasip-fellows">{{cite web|title=EURASIP Fellows|url=https://eurasip.org/eurasip-fellows/|website=EURASIP|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
* [[CNRS Silver Medal]] in 2010<ref name="cnrs-ins2i">{{cite web|title=Éric Moulines|url=https://www.ins2i.cnrs.fr/en/person/eric-moulines|website=CNRS Informatics (INS2I)|publisher=Centre national de la recherche scientifique|access-date=21 April 2026|language=en}}</ref>
* [[IEEE]] Signal Processing Magazine Best Paper Award in 2005, with Olivier Cappé, Jean-Christophe Pesquet, [[Athina Petropulu]] and Xueshi Yang, for "Long-Range Dependence and Heavy-Tail Modeling for Teletraffic Data"<ref name="ieee-sps-magazine-best-paper">{{cite web|title=IEEE Signal Processing Society Signal Processing Magazine Best Paper Award|url=https://signalprocessingsociety.org/sites/default/files/uploads/community_involvement/awards/SPS_Mag_Best_Paper.pdf|website=IEEE Signal Processing Society|format=PDF|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
* IEEE Signal Processing Society Best Paper Award in 1997, with Pierre Duhamel, Jean-François Cardoso and Sylvie Mayrargue, for "Subspace Methods for the Blind Identification of Multichannel FIR Filters"<ref name="ieee-sps-best-paper">{{cite web|title=IEEE Signal Processing Society Best Paper Award|url=https://signalprocessingsociety.org/sites/default/files/uploads/get_involved/awards/Best_Paper.pdf|website=IEEE Signal Processing Society|format=PDF|access-date=21 April 2026}}</ref>
